name: scope-gate-v2
declared: 2026-10-08, before the wording change was written or run
supersedes: scope-gate-v1 wording only (v1 left unchanged and reproducible)
purpose: Offline: make the gate's clarification and conditional text readable for a merchant by naming the guide's own section titles instead of bare codes and phrases. Gate decisions (which claims are flagged, kept, conditionalised or withheld) must not change.

wording.clarification: Your question does not say which type of dispute this is. The rules I found apply only to specific disputes, for example: <up to 3 section titles>. Which reason code or dispute type is your chargeback?
wording.conditional_prefix: Only if your dispute is <one section title>:
wording.title_source: for each flagged cited passage, the deepest heading below chapter level that contains a code or phrase the detector flagged; verbatim, whitespace-normalised; ranked by number of flagged cited passages, then alphabetical; at most 3 in the clarification, 1 per claim in the prefix (the most frequent among that claim's passages)

inputs: Same as scope-gate-v1: 40 citation-valid baseline answers plus the E22 flagged-answer-v1 attempt. No model call, no holdout.

thresholds.W1: Gate decisions identical to v1: same action per answer, same claims withheld or conditionalised, 38 unchanged byte-identical
thresholds.W2: Every section title in any output appears verbatim in a heading of a passage that the answer cited and the detector flagged
thresholds.W3: Clarification text is at most 70 words and names at least 1 and at most 3 titles
thresholds.W4: Every gated output passes validate_answer, quotes unchanged; two runs give identical hashes
thresholds.W5: No clarification or prefix contains a bare qualifier list (no standalone reason-code number list outside a title)

decision_rule: Pass only if W1 to W5 hold. Readability is judged by me, which is not independent; it is reported with the printed E13 and E22 outputs, not thresholded.
limits: Section titles are the publisher's; some are still jargon
Readability is an assisted judgement and needs merchants to confirm
